title: What is a stock?
text: A stock is ownership in a company. Returns come from price moves and dividends. Prices can rise or fall.

title: What is an ETF?
text: An ETF is a fund that holds many assets and trades like a stock. Often tracks an index and has low fees.

title: Diversification
text: Spread investments across many holdings to reduce the impact of any one position. It cannot remove all risk.

title: Risk types
text: Market, company, liquidity, interest-rate, and inflation risk. Understand them before investing.

title: Asset allocation
text: Mix of stocks, bonds, and cash that matches goals, time horizon, and risk tolerance.

title: Dollar-cost averaging
text: Invest a fixed amount on a schedule regardless of price to reduce timing risk.

title: Price vs total return
text: Price return ignores dividends. Total return includes dividends with reinvestment.

title: Real vs nominal return
text: Nominal is raw percent change. Real adjusts for inflation and purchasing power.

title: Small vs large cap
text: Small-caps can grow faster and swing more. Large-caps are often more stable.

title: Growth vs value
text: Growth focuses on fast-growing firms. Value looks for lower prices vs fundamentals.

title: International diversification
text: Owning foreign markets reduces home bias but adds currency and policy risks.

title: What is a bond?
text: A loan to a company or government that pays interest and returns principal at maturity.

title: Expense ratio
text: The annual fee charged by a fund. Lower fees can improve long-term outcomes.

title: Dividend yield
text: Yearly dividend per share divided by price. Dividends can change and are not guaranteed.

title: Tracking error
text: The difference between a fund’s return and its benchmark due to fees and implementation.

title: Reading a fund page
text: Check objective, index, fees, holdings, sector weights, distributions, and risk notes.

title: IPO
text: An Initial Public Offering lists shares on an exchange. Early trading may be volatile.

title: Options (concept)
text: Calls and puts grant rights to buy or sell. Complex and risky. Not for beginners or minors.

title: Short selling (concept)
text: Selling borrowed shares to profit if price falls. Advanced; losses can be unlimited.

title: Leveraged/inverse ETFs
text: Amplify or reverse daily index moves. Short-term tools with higher risk and fees.

title: Duration
text: For bond funds, duration estimates sensitivity to interest-rate changes.

title: REIT
text: Real estate investment trust that owns or finances properties and often pays distributions.

title: Sharpe ratio
text: Return above the risk-free rate divided by volatility. Higher was better historically.

title: Max drawdown
text: Worst peak-to-trough drop. Shows potential pain during declines.

title: Stop-loss
text: Order that sells if price hits a level. May trigger on noise; use with care.

title: Rebalancing
text: Reset to target mix on a schedule or when bands are breached to keep risk level steady.

title: Scam red flags
text: Guaranteed returns, pressure to act fast, secrecy, and odd payment methods.

title: Paper trading
text: Practice without real money to learn mechanics and test strategies.

title: Taxes vary by country
text: Returns may be taxed as income or capital gains. Check local rules.

title: Teen safety
text: Learn with simulations. Discuss real accounts with a parent or guardian. Protect personal info.

title: What is volatility?
text: How much a price moves. Higher volatility means bigger swings and uncertain outcomes.

title: What is liquidity?
text: Ability to trade quickly near last price. Narrow bid-ask spreads help reduce cost.

title: What is bid-ask spread?
text: Difference between buy and sell quotes. Narrow spreads usually lower trading cost.

title: What is market cap?
text: Share price times shares outstanding. Used to group companies by size.

title: What is free cash flow?
text: Cash from operations minus capital expenditure. Funds dividends and debt reduction.

title: What is P/E ratio?
text: Price divided by earnings per share. Lower can imply cheaper, context matters.

title: What is EV/EBITDA?
text: Enterprise value relative to operating earnings. Compares across capital structures.

title: What is beta?
text: Sensitivity to market moves. Beta above 1 tends to move more than the market.

title: What is alpha?
text: Return beyond what market exposure explains. Hard to achieve consistently.

title: DCA vs lump sum
text: DCA spaces buys to cut timing risk; lump sum invests all at once. Both have trade-offs.

title: Order types
text: Market, limit, and stop orders control execution and price. Limits may not fill.

title: Settlement (T+1/T+2)
text: Trades settle after trade date. Funds may not be usable until settlement.

title: After-hours liquidity
text: Lower volume and wider spreads. Use limit orders to control price.

title: Company-specific risk
text: News or execution issues can move a single stock a lot. Diversify to reduce impact.

title: Sector concentration
text: Owning only one industry increases risk if that sector falls.

title: Index tracking
text: Broad index funds provide market exposure with low cost and turnover.

title: Recession concept
text: Broad economic slowdown. Markets can drop before, during, or after.

title: Inflation concept
text: General price increases over time. Erodes purchasing power.

title: Interest rates concept
text: Rates reflect cost of money. Rising rates can pressure bond prices.

title: FX risk
text: Currency changes can amplify or reduce returns on foreign assets.

title: Hedging basics
text: Hedged funds reduce currency swings but may add cost.
